purpose: Re-verdict the 5000ms latency budget on the PER-INVOCATION basis the requester actually stated (one page: generation + the comparison/tests for that same page), replacing the invalid sum-across-5-specs basis used in index-hoist-landed.json.

scopeCorrectionAccepted.requesterWords: I need this to run sub 5 seconds the recreate tool itself and the tests
scopeCorrectionAccepted.priorBasis: sum of generation across 5 unrelated specs vs a single-run 5000ms limit
scopeCorrectionAccepted.reasonOnTheMerits: A sum-of-N budget is invalid by construction: adding a sixth spec would register as a regression without any code becoming slower. The limit is a per-invocation latency, so the denominator of the comparison must be one page.
scopeCorrectionAccepted.testsInterpretation: The phrase and the tests is read as the per-page comparison (backtest compare_once), not the 28-fixture corpus wall time, per explicit instruction 2. Chosen because it is the only test cost attributable to a single page.

premiseCorrections.finding: STALE. Commit 738b96c already unbroke it. backtest built and ran qualification twice from the main tree, exit 0 on the clean run, 0 bytes stderr. No byte-copy workaround was needed.

premiseCorrections.claim: My own prior arm-B per-spec generation medians (live-r15 2235, fluid-r1 2034, fluid-r5 4039, review 3031, recreate-output 1031).
premiseCorrections.finding: INFLATED BY THE HARNESS. Those used Start-Process with stdout/stderr redirection, which adds 350-880ms of process-launch overhead and quantizes near 1000ms. Direct invocation of the same binary on the same specs gives 1825/1805/3608/2029/150. recreate-output was 1031ms reported vs 150ms actual - 85% of the reported figure was harness, not tool.
premiseCorrections.consequence: The ~900ms noise band I previously reported was mostly instrument, not host. Correcting the instrument shrank the worst-spec sd from ~900 to 319ms and made the median verdict decidable.

premiseCorrections.claim: A detached worktree is a safe place to run qualification.
premiseCorrections.finding: FALSE FOR THIS CORPUS. A worktree at 559ca02 contains only 9 fixtures / 26 mutants; 19 fixtures are uncommitted fixture-author work living only in the main tree. My second qualification run, taken in the worktree, reported 26 mutants / 35 comparisons - a SHRUNKEN DENOMINATOR - and was discarded as void, not reported as a result.
premiseCorrections.consequence: Corpus qualification must be run from the main tree until the 19 fixtures are committed. A worktree run silently improves ratios by removing work from the bottom.

premiseCorrections.claim: focus-behavior control FAIL 1 seen in my first run is a regression.
premiseCorrections.finding: FLAKY, NOT A REGRESSION. Re-run from the same tree gave 72/72 passed and 0 failures. Reported, not repaired - it is not my work item.
premiseCorrections.artifact: viewport-pixels hash 2eb034c9fa9b to f57ba70865c0, run 1 only

runs.note: DISCARDED - worktree corpus, shrunken denominator, not a result

perPageComparisonCost.instrument: qualify costLines[].wallMs - one compare_once per fixture unit, the per-page comparison cost
perPageComparisonCost.rejectedInstrument: 28-fixture qualification wall time (170055ms) - the whole corpus, not one page, explicitly excluded
perPageComparisonCost.agreement: Two independent 72-sample runs agree to 39ms at the median - the comparison cost is stable.

generationCost.instrument: direct invocation of the release binary, 5 rounds x 5 specs, stopwatch around the process

verdictPerInvocation.formula: generation median for the spec + per-page comparison median (527ms)
verdictPerInvocation.overall: MET at the typical invocation for all 5 of 5 specs.
verdictPerInvocation.genuinelyInsideOrMerelyClose: GENUINELY INSIDE, but narrowly. The margin is 865ms = 2.20 combined sigma (one-sided p = 0.014), and the 95% CI upper bound of 4907ms falls 93ms below the limit. This is outside the host-noise band, so the measurement DOES decide the median case. It would not have been decidable against my earlier ~900ms noise figure; correcting the Start-Process instrument is what made it decidable.

upperTail.reasoning: 5260 vs 5000 is 0.66 sigma above the limit, inside the noise band. The measurement CANNOT decide the tail case at n=5.
upperTail.whatWouldSettleIt: Variance-limited, therefore reducible by sampling: n = [(Z0.975+Z0.80)*sigma/delta]^2 = [(1.96+0.84)*394/260]^2 = 18 runs per spec resolves a 260ms difference at 95%/80%. About 6 minutes of wall time.

hostContention.statement: The host is shared and saturated; every timing is a contaminated UPPER bound, so a MET verdict is conservative and a MISSED verdict is not.
hostContention.quietHost: Not obtainable - peers are actively building in this tree. Mitigated instead by removing the dominant instrument artifact (Start-Process) and by pooling 144 comparison samples across two runs.

residual.question: After the Index hoist, what is the largest remaining phase in the worst spec?
residual.instrument: RECREATE_TIMING env-gated markers already present at HEAD; 3 instrumented runs. No code was added.
residual.clockCorrection: generate_* and project_* use two different Instant clocks. A naive subtraction across them understates the assets phase; figures below are computed on the correct per-clock basis.
residual.rootCauseMeasured: NOT computation. fluid-r5 declares 18 remote asset URLs pointing at http://localhost:8261 - the capture-time server, which is dead. assets_remote::download attempts them and stalls on connection-refused. A single refused TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:8261 on this host measures 2092ms (dual-stack IPv6 to IPv4 fallback), accounting for essentially the whole 2412ms phase. Only 8 asset files are emitted, all from inline base64; all 18 remote fetches fail.
residual.amdahlBound: If the assets phase went to zero, fluid-r5 generation falls 3552 to 1140ms and the per-invocation total falls 4135 to 1667ms, a 2.5x improvement that also brings the upper tail decisively inside budget.
residual.aimedNextFix: Bound or short-circuit the remote-asset fetch when the capture origin is unreachable (cap the connect timeout, or skip capture-origin localhost URLs once the first connect is refused). This is I/O stall removal, not algorithmic work, and is independent of the css_base cost that dominated live-r15.
residual.contrastWithPriorProfile: generation-profile.json (4c8ae61, live-r15) named css_base at 67.2%. For fluid-r5 at 559ca02 css_base is 46ms. The dominant phase is spec-dependent; there is no single hot spot across the corpus.

consoleErrors.generationRuns: 0 bytes stderr across all 40 generation invocations

newBaseline.supersedes: index-hoist-landed.json arm-B medians, which were harness-inflated

decision: APPROVE - the 5000ms per-invocation budget is MET for all 5 specs at the typical invocation, worst case fluid-r5 at 4135ms with a 95% CI upper bound of 4907ms. The upper tail (5260ms) is NOT met and is not resolvable at n=5; it is reported as indeterminate rather than shaded to either side.
